literature_notes: Both ledger lines (L1, L2) describe the same paper (PMC3123356). L1 explicitly names pEGFP-N1 and p3×FLAG-CMV-14, both of which append the tag to the protein C-terminus. The computed topology places the C-terminus (residues 146–205) in the intracellular compartment, so these are intracellular tags and do not qualify as surface sites. L2 additionally mentions a myc-tagged construct, but the clip states no residue number and no terminus assignment for the myc tag; the position is therefore unstated and the site cannot be pinned (rule: 'a commercial plasmid whose tag POSITION is unstated; you cannot pin insert_after_residue'). Even if myc were inferred to be N-terminal (extracellular), the clip provides no junction residue and the topology-derived rule requires that exactly one extracellular terminus be unambiguous — here the myc placement is genuinely ambiguous between N- and C-terminal vectors. No ledger line supports any extracellular insertion. Zero sites is the correct answer.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal GFP (pEGFP-N1) and 3×FLAG (p3×FLAG-CMV-14) fusions are tolerated and confirm membrane expression, but the C-terminus (residues 146–205) is intracellular per the computed topology.
